speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Sahana bhavato sahano bhunakto sahaviryam karavavahai te Jasvinavadhitamastuma vidvishavahai Om Shanti Shanti Shanti Om Yam Brahma Varunendra Rudra anti devyastavaih vedaih sangapadakramopanishadaih gayanti samsaragah dhyanavati Sthita yasyam tam na vidu surasuraganah devayat devayat So in the first chapter, Arjuna gives all the reasons why they should not fight the war. He almost collapses on the chariot. Bhagwan uses some lashing words to wake him up. Arjuna again repeats the same arguments. How can I fight with my teacher, with the elders? I think it is better to beg and live than kill these noble ones. But then Arjuna himself realizes that there is a deep confusion within.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: What is dharma, what is adharma, what is right, what is wrong, what should be done, what should not be done. He realizes his confusion, but one great thing Arjuna does is, he completely surrenders unto Bhagwan. The first chapter is called Arjuna Vishada Yoga. Now a question may come, how can Vishada be considered Yoga? Vishada means sorrow. Yoga is a science of uniting with the Lord. How can sorrow be considered a yoga? But then the answer given is, it is because of this sorrow that Arjuna surrendered unto Bhagwan. It is because of this sorrow that Arjuna sought this greatest knowledge.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: So therefore, even this sorrow, is a blessing in disguise. Even this sorrow is an auspicious beginning. It is not inauspicious, though superficially it may appear to be inauspicious. So even this vishada is considered to be yoga because vishada opens up the door. towards yoga. So then Arjuna surrenders completely to Bhagwan, saying Bhagwan, I am absolutely helpless. Though I have all the talents and abilities to fight the war, but these talents I am not able to bring it out. because of utter helplessness, born out of confusion regarding what is dharma and what is adharma. So therefore Bhagwan, nishchitam shreyah, whatever it is, please tell me.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Whatever is ultimately good for me, ultimately good for all. For all times, whatever it is, please tell me, please guide me. Shishyasteham shadhimaam tvam prapannam. I completely surrender unto you. I am your disciple. I don't know anything. Please teach me. I want this knowledge because the sorrow which I am experiencing now, this sorrow can never go with any kind of external. adjustments. I may be given the Lordship over the entire heaven, over all the gods. I may be given a kingdom which is unrivaled and prosperous, but even then this sorrow which is burning, all my senses, this sorrow will not go away.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: So Bhagwan, please teach me, please guide me. Saying this, Arjuna kept quiet, saying I am not going to fight. Na yotsye. So now, what does Bhagwan do? Let us chant the next verse. Tamu vacha Rishi Keshah prahasanniva Bharata. Senayorubhayor madhye vishidantamidam vachaha. So now this is the condition of Arjuna, he is quiet. He's determined not to fight and he has sought for the highest knowledge. Now Bhagwan looking at this condition of Arjuna. What is the condition of Arjuna? Senayor ubhayor madhye vishidantam. The middle of the two armies. What is the condition of Arjuna? Vishidantam, drowning in sorrow.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Looking at him. Bhagwan Rishikeshah, the master of the senses, the supreme Lord, prahasan iva, smilingly. smilingly idam vachah uvacha. Bhagwan spoke these words. Now see the condition here. On one side Arjuna is grieving, crying, on the other side Bhagwan is smiling. Situation is the same. You just see how Two different people are reacting to the same situation. One is crying, other is smiling. Now a question may come, why is Bhagwan smiling? Prahasanniva, prahasan means smiling. Now the question may come, why Bhagwan is smiling? The answer comes in the next verse actually. But there can be so many reasons why Bhagwan is smiling.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Reason number one. Just bring into the picture how Arjuna entered into the war field. What did he say? Bhagwan, take the chariot. into the center field. The center of the two armies. Let me see how many people have come to fight. Who all have come to fight. Now at that time he was full of confidence, courage, fearlessness, bold. This was the Arjuna who entered into the battlefield. Now what is the condition of Arjuna? Totally grieving and crying. There's a stark contrast between the Arjuna who entered into the field and now the condition of Arjuna. It is something like You know, during Diwali days, you have these firecrackers.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: So there's a huge bomb or some big firecracker. So everybody is expecting something huge. Horrible sound everybody is expecting. So now you light that firecracker. So you have that string. So now it has caught fire. Now the sparks are coming. Everyone has run away from there. Some of them have closed their ears also. And then what happens? Some sounds, gone. Isn't it? This is the condition of Arjuna. World number one warrior coming there to fight and now it is crying. I will not fight. This may be one reason why Bhagwan smiled. Another reason why Bhagwan smiled is because as we all know, Arjuna is a very close friend of Bhagwan.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: So here was this Arjuna throughout his life, he was running around for so many kinds of vidyas. Dhanurvidya, Astravidya, Shastravidya, throughout his life he was busy acquiring varieties of vidyas including Gandharva Vidya. He got this Gandharva Vidya the knowledge about science, I mean what is that? music, dance, etcetera. He got it from Swargaloka. His teacher was Chitrasena. He knows how to dance, how to play tabla, mritangam, everything he knows. So throughout his life he was busy with all kinds of apara vidyas. Now for the first time, he is showing interest in Paravidya or Atma Vidya or Brahma Vidya.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: So Bhagwan was very happy. This might be another reason why Bhagwan is smiling. You want your loved ones to gain the highest, to gain the best. Very many times it happens. The husband or the wife attend satsang, they are attending all Gita classes, but their spouse is just the opposite. Husband is there in the class, wife just doesn't like it. Or wife loves this kind of spiritual discourses, husband is just the opposite. Very rarely we find husband and wife together liking this. So very many times what happens is, The one person who loves this, who knows this value, wants the beloved also to gain this knowledge because this is the best, isn't it?

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: So now Bhagwan, because his dearest friend is Arjuna, Bhagwan smiles because he was happy that at least now he's showing interest. in this knowledge. This is another reason why Bhagwan might have smiled. There can be one more reason also. What is that reason? When the patient comes to the doctor, crying, weeping, anxious, worried, describing his physical problems. Not knowing what to do, not knowing what kind of disease he's suffering from. And as this patient is describing the symptoms, the diseases of the body. The doctor as he's listening to these, when the doctor comes to know that, oh, this person is suffering from this, what will the doctor do?

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: The doctor will smile, isn't it? Why that smile? The problem with which he's suffering from, I have the solution. When you have the solution, you smile. When you don't have the solution, you weep. So here is Arjuna weeping and crying because he doesn't know the solution. Here is Bhagwan smiling because he knows what Arjuna is going through. He exactly knows what solution alone can solve this Arjuna disease. That may be one more reason why Bhagwan is smiling. Anyway, Bhagwan smiled and he spoke these words. Now from the next words onwards, real Teaching of Bhagavad Gita starts.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Bhagwan starts with a powerful verse, a very, very famous verse. Let us chant verse number 11. Shri Bhagavanuvacha, Ashochyananvashochastvam. Prajnavadaancha bhashase gataasu nagataasuccha nanu shochanti panditaah Yes. Bhagavad Gita begins with a bang, as they say. What is that bang? Bhagwan smiles, and this is one reason why Bhagwan smiles. Arjuna, actually Bhagwan is making fun of Arjuna. Arjuna, tvam anva shochah, you are grieving. A shochyan, you are grieving for the ungrievable, for those whom. You should not grieve for Ashochyan. You are grieving for the ungrievable. At the same time, on one side you are grieving, on the other side Prajnavadascha bhashase.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: You are speaking the words of wisdom. You are speaking like a wise man. So on one On one side you are speaking like a wise man, on the other side you are grieving. Look at that contrast. Arjuna, shall I tell you one thing? Panditaha na anushochante. The sign of the Wise. The indications of the wise, the sign of wisdom is the wise man never grieves. Gatasun agatasun with regard to gata asun. Gata asu, asu means prana. Life breath is called asu. So gata asu means what? Those from whom the life breath has gone away, meaning dead people.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Gatasun, dead people, Agatasun. Agatasun means what? Not yet dead. still breathing or dying or living. With respect to the living people or non-living people, Panditaha na anushochanti, the wise people don't grieve. This is the sign of wisdom. So what is the sign of wisdom? Absence of grief is the sign of wisdom. Absence of sorrow is the sign of wisdom. Peace, happiness, cheerfulness is the sign of wisdom. Arjuna, In your case, it is very clear. On one side you are speaking as though you are a wise man, on the other side what are you doing? You are crying.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: What does it mean? It simply means you are otherwise, not wise. It simply means whatever you are saying is wrong. A person who is wise, he will have right understanding about life. And because he has right understanding about life, his analysis about life situation will be perfect, it will be right. He will have right analysis of the situations of life, of the problems, of the challenges of life, his analysis will be perfect. And because of perfect analysis, his decisions will be perfect. And because of perfect decisions, his actions will be perfect. And those people who perform perfect actions can never grieve.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: A person with right understanding about life will have right analysis. Right analysis will lead to right decisions. Right decisions will lead to right actions. For such people who perform right actions, where is the question of grief? Such a person alone can be peaceful in this world, happy in this world. Arjuna, the very fact that you are grieving shows your knowledge is imperfect. Your analysis is imperfect. Your decision is imperfect. Your actions are imperfect. The beauty of the verse is, Bhagwan is here a perfect teacher. What is the job of the teacher? The job of the teacher is, place the finger exactly where it pains, where the problem is.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Pinpoint the mistake. This is the job of the teacher. The shishya is wrong somewhere because of his wrong judgements, wrong knowledge, he is suffering. What is the job of the teacher? Where exactly are you wrong? But the first step is to prove that the shishya is wrong. My dear Arjuna, you are wrong. What is the proof? The very, the very fact that you are crying proves that you are wrong. Now Bhagwan is going to explain why Arjuna is wrong, where Arjuna has made the mistake. The term used here is Panditaha. Na anushochanti. The wise people, they don't grieve.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Now the common meaning which is prevalent in the society regarding Pandita is some priest in temple. Whenever we hear the term Pandit, We think some priest in the temple. So here Bhagwan Shankaracharya as he makes it very clear who is a pandita. Panda, atma vishaya buddhihi yasyam. Te panditah. Those who have Panda is called Pandita. Now what is this Panda? Panda means the knowledge about the self. Those who know who they are, that knowledge about the supreme self is called Panda, and those who have Panda, they are called as Pandita. So now what is Bhagwan trying to indicate, Arjuna?

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: All your sorrow is because you don't know who you are. All your sorrow is because of a mistaken identity with regard to yourself. So if you want to put an end to your sorrow, there is only one way, know thyself. This is the message. Now, very interestingly, Bhagwan Shankaracharya has not written any commentary up to 10th verse. First chapter Bhagwani, silence, second chapter up to 10th verse, Bhagwan Shankaracharya has not written any commentary, but after this, he writes a huge commentary. Summarizing what is the problem with which Arjuna is suffering. Now let us discuss that point.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: The first mistake we all commit is Ignorance with regard to our own true nature. Everything starts from agnana. What is our true nature? We are Sat, Chit, Anand. We are existence, consciousness, bliss. This is our true nature. Sat means existence. Chit means consciousness. Anand means bliss. This is our true nature. But when we don't know our true nature, that ignorance of our true nature is called agyanam. Agyanam. Not agnanam with regard to the worldly knowledge, no. Agnanam regarding our own true identity. All problems starts from here. Agnanam. I don't know who I am. So what is the next?

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: So from this mistake, what is the next mistake we commit? Naturally, I want to know who I am. So now I start using inference. Through my own superficial analysis of my life, I try to. Know myself, understand myself. So what do I do? I look upon myself and what do I find? Whatever is happening in this body, I am able to experience. Whatever is happening outside this body, I am not able to experience. Therefore, I am limited to this body. See this. If there is a pain in this body, I am able to experience. If there is a pain in somebody's body, I am not able to experience.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Therefore, this body is mine, that body is not mine. Whatever is within the limitations, within the boundaries of this body, I am experiencing it. Whether it is heat or cold, whether it is joy or sorrow, within the boundaries of this body I am experiencing, outside the boundary I am not experiencing. So what is my limit? My limit is this body. Now slowly, slowly I start defining myself as this body. Not only my direct experience, but by inference also, I try to define myself as this body. How? Somebody is born. Somebody is born means what? Physical body is born.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: And now that person is available for interaction in this world, and the physical body is dead, that person is no more available for interaction. What does it mean? That person exists with the existence of that body, that person no more exists with the non-existence of that body. This I see in others. I'm not seeing in myself. I'm seeing in others. So with the existence of the body, that person is existing, with the non-existence of the body, that person is no more existing. Therefore the same thing should be true with me also. Meaning what? I exist with this body, I die with this body.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Therefore, I am this body. This is called inference. So how do I define myself? I define myself as this body. This is the second mistake coming from the primary mistake. What is the first mistake? Ajnanam, I don't know myself, I want to know myself, so how do I define myself? I define myself as the body. I am the body. This is called Dehatma Bhava. Deha itself is Atma, body itself is me, that is called Dehatma, Dehatma Bhava. So this understanding comes now. I am the body. This is the second step. Now, what kind of desires we will have?

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Our desires will always be based on our true nature. What is our true nature? Sat Chit. Ananda is our true nature, based on that true nature alone we will have desire. So what will be our desire? Our desire will be to exist. All of us we want to exist. We don't want to die. We want to live. From where did the desire come from? The desire has come because our Atma, the supreme self is Sat. Sat means existence. That which is always existing. That which can never become non-existent, that is the nature of the self and that is actually my nature.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: So, I will always have the desire to exist, but now my definition of myself is I am the body. So what will be my definition of existence? As long as the body exists, I exist, so let me protect the body. Let me preserve the body. Let me do everything to live ever and ever in the body. Isn't it? Let me not grow old. Let me do everything at least to postpone old age if not prevent. Everything I will do because my definition of myself is this body. So I will try to exist through the body.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: I will try to experience happiness. Now again this is another desire. What is the desire? I want to be happy forever and ever and ever. Where did this desire come from? It has come from my true nature. What is my true nature? Ananda Swarupa is my true nature. I am Sachit Ananda. Infinite bliss is my true nature. Happiness is my true nature. So naturally I will try to desire happiness. But now since my definition of myself is the body, so what kind of happiness will I seek? I will seek happiness through the body. I will seek happiness of the body.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Anything which makes the body comfortable, happy, cheerful, that I will do. How will I get the knowledge? Chit means consciousness, chit means knowledge also. So I will try to grab all that knowledge, I will try to gain all that knowledge which will give me sat. which will give me Anand. Because I want to exist forever, I want to exist happily forever, I want to exist with infinite happiness, infinite joy, infinite peace. This is what I desire, but the mistake is I will keep on desiring it in and through the body because I consider myself as the body.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Now, so what is the first step? Ajnana. What is the next one? Dehatma bhava. With the dehatma bhava. Now that you consider yourself to be the body, now that you consider your existence. as nothing but the existence of the body, naturally the third step will come. The third step is raga. Raga means attachment. You'll be attached to the body. Why are you attached to the body? Because it is this body which is giving me existence. It is this body which is giving me happiness. And therefore, since I am craving for existence and happiness, and it is this body which is giving me Therefore, naturally what will happen?

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: There will be raga, that is the third one. Raga means attachment. Primary raga is with the body, secondary ragas is with everything connected to the body which will give me security, which will give me happiness. So therefore, I will have attachment not only with the body, I will also have attachment to everything connected to the body which gives the body happiness, which gives the body existence. So what are they? It can be wealth. It can be power, it can be position, it can be relatives, it can be house, everything. But they are all secondary attachments.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: What is the primary attachment? The body. They are all there, they are capable of giving happiness to this body. They are capable of giving security to this body, therefore they are lovable. So what comes? Raga comes. What is raga? Attachment. Now wherever there is raga, there has to be dwesha. You can't avoid it. Raga means what? Likes. Dwesha means dislikes. You like something, someone or some situation because it is capable of giving happiness to you. You don't like something, someone, or some situation because they give sorrow to you. Raga and Dwesha, they are the two sides of the same coin.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: You cannot have only Raga, no Dwesha, impossible. Greater the intensity of raga, equally great will be the intensity of dwesha. If you want to get rid of raga, you will have to get rid of dwesha also. Raga dwesha, they always come in pairs. So what are the steps now? Number one, agnana. Number two, dehatma bhava. Number three, raga dwesha. Now what happens when the mind is filled with raga dwesha? So what is raga dwesha? I am attached to everything that gives me security and happiness and comfort and peace. I am repelled by everything that threatens my existence, that threatens my happiness.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: So now what is the state of the mind? The mind is filled with raga dwesha. What will be the natural consequence? The natural consequence is wherever the mind is filled with likes and dislikes, such a mind will always experience delusion, which is called as Moha. Moha. Moha means delusion. What do you mean delusion? The inability to see what is is called delusion. You see what is not there, you don't see what is there. This is called delusion. A mind which is filled with raga dwesha will be a mind which will be deluded. They go together.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Greater the raga dwesha, greater will be the delusion. And this is exactly what Arjuna is experiencing. What do you mean raga dwesha leads to delusion? Some examples will make it clear. What is delusion? The inability to see the truth as it is is called delusion. Why are you unable to see the truth? You are unable to see the truth because raga colors the reality. Another meaning of raga is color. In Sanskrit, this is another meaning, dye, D Y E. Raga means that also. We are not talking of musical raga. Raga has so many meanings. In music also there is a raga, not that.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: So now a mind which is filled with raga dwesha will color your mind and with a colored mind, You will not be able to see the truth as it is. What kind of truth you will see? You will see a colored truth. You will see a distorted truth. Examples will make it clear now. What is the example? So here is a judge. He's supposed to judge impartially. Now his own son, his most beloved son has been caught by the police as a criminal and now he's standing there. Now the father, the judge, he has to judge.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: But he loves his son extremely. So now naturally what happens? Now this raga will start interfering with his sense of impartiality, sense of judgement. So what will he say? To err is human, to forgive is divine. Why? Because this is my son. Now see, this is called Moha, you know. You tend to analyze a situation compelled by your raga dweshas. This is what happens. Raga dwesha paralyzes your intellect, paralyzes your discriminating ability. So this Arjuna disease is a disease which we are all suffering from somewhere or the other. A teacher who is correcting the papers.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: And now as she is correcting, she comes to know that oh this paper is my own son's paper. Now as a teacher what is she supposed to do? She has to give marks impartially, if the answer is right, she should give full marks, if the answer is wrong, she should not give marks. Now, Through the handwriting she has understood 10th, what you call, standard exam paper. Through the handwriting she understood this is my son's paper. Now what will she tend to do? She will tend to give more marks, isn't it? This is my son. Now see the conflict here.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: The teacher in me wants to be impartial, the mother in me wants to be partial towards my own son. Now there is a conflict here. Now this is called Arjuna disease. Attachment towards my son is not allowing me to remain impartial. That's why in Chinmaya Mission we never allow these parents as judges during Bhagavad Gita chanting competition. You understand? If the judge is his mother, her child is chanting Bhagavad Gita. It is said wherever, what is that? Where love is thick, fault is thin. is a saying. Where love is thick, fault is thin. So naturally when she hears her child chanting Bhagavad Gita, she will not see any of these faults, only nice nice things she will hear.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: This is the handicap of an intellect which is suffering from the virus of attachment. It just wants to listen what is pleasing to it. It just wants to see what is pleasing to it. It sees the truth in a distorted way. It sees the truth according to its own convenience. Another example. Mother child example is the best example because the mother is the one who is so attached to the child. She does everything foolish for the child. So there is this drama competition going on. Her child is there as one of the character in the drama.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: So in the drama there is this king, there is this queen, there is this minister, there is this hero, heroine, so many things are there and her child is there in a corner. Holding one spear, he is the gatekeeper in a corner. He has no role. His only role is to hold this. Now this mother is clicking what you call that camera. Now everybody has got a camera now. So now the mother is focusing, where will she focus? Will she focus the center stage where all important things are happening? No, automatically, helplessly, spontaneously. Her camera will go towards that fellow who is standing in the corner, doing nothing, looking here there.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Isn't it? Who will be the center character in her camera? Not the king who is sitting in the central stage, but the fellow who is in the corner. After the drama you ask that mother, Amma, what was the story about in that drama? She is not aware. The only thing I know is this fellow is there standing as a guard. Maybe he is the most important fellow. Are you able to understand how this raga makes you moodha, the one who is having moha is called moodha. Raga, intense attachment makes you paralyzed, you are helpless. You are not able to think clearly.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: What is very clearly visible for others, you are not able to see. not able to see. You are in your own hallucination, your own imagination. You have created a castle of foolishness where you are the king. This is Moha. You are seeing what is not there, you are not seeing what is there. And this is exactly what Arjuna is facing now. He is actually a Kshatriya. What is his duty? To fight against unrighteousness, to fight for righteousness, that is his duty. He has come to the war field as a Kshatriya, as an army man. He has not come to the war field as a family man.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Now what is he doing? His all arguments are the arguments of a family man, not as an army man. See that. All of us we have different roles to play in the society. Some roles are higher, some roles are lower. The roles which are connected to the nation, those roles are higher roles. For example, Arjuna, his higher role is the role in which he has to discharge the responsibility, keeping in mind. The citizens of the nation, that's a bigger role. The army role is a bigger role, family role is a smaller role. When there is a conflict between the bigger role and the smaller role, which one should you adopt?

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Whenever there is a conflict. Now exactly that is happening in Arjuna's case. The family role is coming in conflict with the bigger role, the army role. Army role asks him to fight, family role asks him to withdraw. Now which one should he take? You should take the bigger role always. You must sacrifice the lower for the sake of the higher. Just like the teacher who is correcting the paper. The teacher in her wants to be impartial, the mother in her wants to be partial. Which role should she take? The teacher role or a mother role?

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: She has to take the teacher role because that role is bigger. That is going to influence the majority of the society in the in the society, isn't it? All of us, we have this conflict in life. This is not something which Arjuna alone is facing. So now what is the mistake Arjuna has done? Now he is acting and thinking. remaining in the family role, not remaining in the army role. This is the mistake he's doing. Higher is discarded for the sake of the lower. So that is why always you will see this term, Swajanam, Swajanam.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: He's constantly saying the same thing, Swajanam. Swajanam means what? My people. I am theirs, they are mine. All these things show how much attached he was, how because of attachment his thinking has gone off. Very many times we experience this. And now, what is the result of this Moha? Moha will force you to do Paradharma. This is the next one. What is not your duty, you will start doing it. What is your duty, you will start escaping from it. You will not do it. Svadharma you will not do, Moha will force you to do paradharma and that is exactly what Arjuna is doing.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Arjuna is saying I will not fight, it is far better if I take go and take bhiksha. Are bhiksha is not your job. Bhiksha is meant for sanyasis. Bhiksha for you is paradharma. What is your swadharma? Your swadharma is to fight, not take bhiksha. It is far better if I go and take bhiksha and live on alms, fool. You are doing paradharma now. A brahmachari has a right to take bhiksha. A sanyasi has a right to take bhiksha. A grihastha has no right to take bhiksha. Especially a kshatriya has absolutely no right to take bhiksha.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Now he's saying, I will do that. See that? It is paradharma. Suppose there is a person, his higher officer, he's forcing him to become corrupt, asking him to take bribes, forcing him to take all the improper, illegal, immoral measures. What should he do? The higher officer is asking him to do. Now this person thinks the pros and cons. If I don't listen to him, if I displease him, what will happen? I will lose my job. If I lose my job, how will I take care of my wife and children? You see that? Very many times people come and describe.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: It's a very, what you call, prestigious job. Thousands and thousands of people are waiting to get that job and you have got it. And unfortunately, you have a boss. What kind of boss? Who is corrupt and who wants you to assist him in his corruption? What will you do? Now suddenly you also will have Arjuna disease. But in majority of the cases there is no disease because happily the person joins hands with him. Then there is no disease then. If you are compromising, then there is no disease. The moment you try to oppose it, go against it.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: No, come what may, I'm not going to compromise with a higher principle, even if the job goes away, it doesn't matter. Lord will take care. If this is your thing, hats off to you. But normally what do we do? Moha is there. If I lose my job, how will I take care of my wife and children? So what to do? Better assist him. Then comes Paradharma. See that? Ajnana. Next one? Dehatma bhavana. Next one? Raga. Next one? Moha, raga dwesha together. Raga dwesha, then moha, next what? Paradharma. What should be the next? The next is choicelessly shoka, sorrow.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: And this is what Arjuna is facing now. See the sequence. When you do what you are not supposed to do, when you compromise with the higher principles of life, when you are unrighteous, helplessly, You will experience only one emotion and that is sorrow. You have no choice. Anyone who compromises with higher values has no choice but to remain miserable. Shoka is the consequence of the wrong actions, of the wrong decisions, of the wrong analysis of life. The end result is Shoka. A person who lives a corrupt life, immoral life, illegal life, look at his condition.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Shoka at three levels, adhyatmika level, adhibhautika level, adhidaivika level, all the levels he will experience only sorrow. When you are corrupt, your own mind is not at peace. That is selfish yoga. When you are corrupt, someday or the other you will be caught. The higher officer is caught along with you are also caught. So what happens? At the aadhi bhautika level also you experience shoka. You are put into jail. All your name, fame, everything gone. In the newspaper, big, big letters your name come. What is that? Nothing but shoka only. Humiliation, isn't it? And there are some news channels, thousands and thousands of time they will show the same thing again and again, again and again.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: They will ensure that the people never forget even after their death. See that? Just imagine the amount of humiliation, that pain which that person is suffering when he sees all this. Shoka at the mind level, Shoka at the worldly level, of course after death also Shoka alone because he has done all adharmic actions. Isn't it? What will be the result? Not Swarga but Naraka only, guarantee. Shoka at all the levels. Now the question is, let us go back. What is the cause of this Shoka? Step by step you go back. The cause of Shoka is Moha.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Cause of Moha is Raga Dwesha. Cause of Raga Dwesha is Cause of Raga Dwesha is Dehatma Bhavana and cause of Devatma Bhavana is Ajnana. So if you want to Uproot shoka. Uproot means what? Once again it should never come. We are not talking of temporary methods. Suppose there's a tree, you keep on clipping the leaves and branches and twigs. The tree is not going to die. If you want to kill that tree, destroy that tree, what you have to do? From the very root, you have to solve the problem, isn't it? In the same way, from the very root, if you have to solve, you have to put an end to the sorrow, shoka, where should you go?

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Go to the root and what is there in the root? Ajnana is there, so therefore now Bhagwan is trying to solve this problem from the root. So what is the only solution for agnana? Gnana is the solution. If the problem is agnana, gnana alone can be the solution. With this purpose, Now Bhagwan enters into Jnana Yoga which is called as Sankhya Yoga. Is it clear? Now let us proceed. With this intention, now Bhagwan is going to give Gnana to Arjuna. What is Gnana? That you are not this body, you are none other than Sachchit Anand Atma.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: This is in short Gnana. This is what Bhagwan is going to give now. Now let us see the next verse. Verse number 12. Natvevaham jato nasam natvam neme janadhipaha. Na chaiva na bhavishyamah sarve vayamatah param. So from here, verse number 12 to 25, Bhagwan gives this self knowledge. And that's why this chapter is named as Sankhya Yoga. What is the meaning of Sankhya? Atma, the supreme self, the knowledge of the supreme self. So from verse number 12 to 25, that is the topic. So what does Bhagwan say? Arjuna, Natu eva aham jatu nasam natvam na ime janadhipaha.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Arjuna, there was never a time when I You or these Janadhipas, these kings were not there. There was never a time when I, you, or these kings who have assembled to fight the war. There was never a time when we were not there. Nachaiva na bhavishyamaha. Sarve vayam atah param. Again, there will never be a time in the future when we will not be there. There was never a time when we were not there. There will never be a time when we will not be there. Meaning what? In the past also we were there. In the present anyway you are seeing we are there.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: In the future also we will be there. What does it mean? It means we are immortal in reality. Actually speaking, there is no death. Disappoint. Arjuna, actually speaking, nobody is going to die. Deathlessness is our nature. Immortality is our nature. Go on, what is the proof? Are your own experience can be your proof. Now Bhagwan gives a beautiful example which can be a proof. for our deathlessness, which is the next verse. Verse number 13. Dehinosmin yatha dehe kaumaram yauvanam jara tatha dehanthara praptihi. Dheeras tatra na mukhyate. Arjuna, look at your own body. Asmin dehe, in this body you can experience that.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Only if you are little observant, little careful. What is happening in your body? Asmin dehe, what is happening? Kaumaram, yauvanam, jara, these are the different stages of the body. Kaumaram, what is called as the childhood. So all of us. We have experienced this state, isn't it? There was a time when the physical body was in that stage of childhood. Then, Yauvanam. You became adult, young. You came to that what you call youth stage, yauvanam. And later on, the very same. Body, Jara, old age. Bhagwan is giving an experiential proof. to indicate that actually speaking we don't die.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: So what is Bhagwan saying, Arjuna, look at your body, constantly it is going from one stage to another. Constantly it is dying, and every time something is dying, something new is coming up. And you are the one who is observing all these changes. Arjuna, do you change? Bodies are changing, but in this process, are you changing? You will find that you remain changeless. You remain a changeless witness to all the changes that are happening at the body level. They say every 6 to 7 years the body completely changes. Every cell is replaced by a new cell, they say.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Meaning a completely new body is given to you. When we were born, we had a body. In our childhood stage, we had a body, another body. When we were young, another body. Now we are old, another body. So what is happening to the bodies? It is being replaced by the other. But what is happening to the observer of these bodies? The possessor of these bodies, the possessor doesn't change. is just a changeless witness to all the changes. Now what does it mean? It simply means you don't die, it is only the body which is dying.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: What is the proof that you are not changing? Only the body is changing. What is the proof? The very fact that you are able to remember the past itself is the proof. You are able to remember the past means what? You who is recollecting in the present is the very same you who has experienced it in the past. Are you able to understand? If the eye of the past is different from the eye of the present, then this eye of the present will never be able to recollect the happenings of the eye of the past.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Got it? The very fact that you are able to connect your present eye with the past eye shows that the present eye itself is the past eye. And that itself proves that this I has never changed. What has changed? Everything connected to, related to, surrounding the I has changed, but the I has never changed. The experiencer is the same, the witness is the same, the observer is the same, the Sakshi is the same. What does it mean? It simply means you are deathless. Now Bhagwan says if this much is true, that each and every body is going and new body is coming, if this much is true, why don't extend this logic to one more step?

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: What is the next step? Tatha deha antara praptihi. This is the next stage. What is the next stage? Body dropping dead. So what should happen to this I, the witness? It should remain. Why? Because all this time when the body was changing, this I remained unchanged. So naturally by logic, what should it lead to? The body will drop dead, but this I will remain unchanged. It is just a logical extension. Even while living bodies are dying so many times, at that time the I remained changeless. So this I will remain changeless even when the physical body drops dead.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Therefore, dheeraha tatra na muhyati. The wise people, dheeraha here doesn't mean courageous man. Dhi, the one who has dhi is called dheera. Dhi means intelligence, wisdom, the man of wisdom. The very same pandita earlier is called as dheera here. Dheeraha tatra na mukhyate. Wise man is never deluded. Regarding what? Regarding the identity about himself. As far as others are concerned, they are all totally deluded. What is the delusion? I am this physical body. Whereas what is the knowledge about this wise man? I am not the body, I am the observer of the body. I am that consciousness in the light of which I am conscious of this body.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Body is an object, I am the subject. The body is the seen, it is a drishya vastu, I am the drashta. This knowledge that dheera purusha, the wise man has. Therefore, there is no delusion. And therefore, there is no grief also. Nanu shochanti panditaha, always related to it. Why do you grieve? You grieve because you think you will die. Actually speaking, there is no death. And when there is no death, why should you grieve? So what is the difference between a wise man and an ignorant man? The difference is only this, wise person knows himself, the ignorant person doesn't know himself.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Arjuna, this is the cause of your sorrow. You don't know who you are. You think you are the body. And in the battlefield, you think you are going to kill so many people or others are going to kill you. You are just looking the whole thing from the bodily standpoint. You're not seeing from the highest standpoint and that is why you are grieving. Whereas a wise person, he never grieves. Why? Because he knows that even when the body dies, I remain deathless. And whatever I need in life, Sat. Existence, chit, consciousness, anand, bliss, everything is the nature of the self.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: So I don't have to beg it from the body, it is already myself. Whatever I need, it is there already in me. So therefore what is the need of Grieving. I want to exist forever and ever and ever. I don't have to desire it because it is my nature. I want infinite happiness. I don't have to desire it because it is my nature. Therefore, dheeraha tatra na mohyati. The wise person is never deluded. So what is the greatness of this wise person? He is holding on to the permanent, giving no much value to the impermanent.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: What is the mistake committed by the ignorant person? He is holding on to the impermanent, never even bothering about the permanent. He doesn't know that there is something called permanent in us. This is the difference. One smiles, the other cries. Bhagwan is smiling, Arjuna is crying. What is the, what makes the difference? knowledge makes a difference. Now how to live with this knowledge in the day-to-day world, that is the next topic. Arjuna, how you should live? That topic. Quick, we will see tomorrow. Om, Sarve Bhavantu Sukhinah, Sarve Santu Niramayah. Sarve bhadrani pashyanto, ma kashchit dukh bhagbhavet.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Asato ma shadgamaya, tamaso ma jyotirgamaya. Mrityorma Amritam Gamaya Om Shanti Shanti Shantihi Harih Om Shri Gurubhyo Namah

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Om Om Sahana bhavatu sahano bhunaktu sahaviryam karavavahai te Om Shanti Shanti Shantihi Om Yam Brahma Varunendra Rudra Marutah Stunvanti Divyai Stavaih Vedai Sangapadakramopanishadaih Dhyanavasthita tadgatena manasa pashyanti yam yoginah yasyantam na vidussuraasuraganah devayu tasmai namah Deva yatastra When Arjuna confessed to Bhagwan about his confusion and when he's completely surrendered unto Bhagwan saying Bhagwan I am confused. Please guide me, please teach me. I am your disciple. I completely surrender unto you. Because this sorrow which I am facing, this sorrow cannot go unless the very understanding in me is rectified, is corrected. Bhagwan smiles, and then the teaching of Bhagavad Gita starts from verse number 11.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: What does Bhagwan say? Bhagwan says, Arjuna, on one side you are talking the words of wisdom, on the other side you are grieving. Grief is not the sign of wisdom. The very fact that you are grieving, The very fact that you are immersed in sorrow, it simply shows your line of thinking is wrong. Your analysis of life is wrong. Really speaking, the wise people, Panditaha, Gatasun, Agatasun cha na anushochanti. The signature of a wise man is, he never grieves. For the people who are living or for the people who are dead. The sign of knowledge, the sign of wisdom is peace.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: The sign of wisdom is cheerfulness, the sign of wisdom is joy, it is happiness. So here Bhagwan uses the term Pandita. Who is a Pandita? The one who has gained the self knowledge is called a Pandita. Pandita is not a scholar. Sometimes Pandit. Sometimes they use this term. for a great musician, for some singer. Sometime they use this term for some scholarly person. But actual meaning of Pandita is the one who has gained the knowledge of the self. This is the way it has to be understood here. Panda. Atma vishaya buddhi yasyam te. The man of self knowledge.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: So Arjuna, it is only the man of self-knowledge who doesn't grieve because he has the right knowledge. Therefore, you must gain this knowledge because it is this lack of self-knowledge which has landed you in this great sorrow. Now how is lack of knowledge connected to sorrow? There Bhagwan Shankaracharya ji writes this commentary which we had seen in detail earlier yesterday. So what is the logic? First is agyana, we don't know who we are. The second is dehatma bhava, since we don't know who we are, we identify ourselves with the body. And thus, we label ourselves as the body.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: I am this body. Now what is the mistake with this? What happens immediately after? With this dehatma bhava comes raga, intense attachment. Number one, attachment to the body. Number two, attachment to everything related to the body. Attachment to everything which can give comforts and conveniences to the body. Everything that can give existence to the body, that can give happiness to the body. Because we are attached to existence and happiness. This attachment finally leads to the attachment to the body and everything related to the body. Wealth, power, position, relatives, etcetera. Now what is the problem with this raga?

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: The problem with raga is, the moment the mind is filled with this raga dwesha, likes and dislikes, such a mind will be unable to see the reality. Raga dwesha distorts the reality. It taints the very vision of the seer. Raga dwesha makes your vision narrow. So you are not able to see the truth. You are only seeing the truth. distorted by your impure mind, the impurity being raga dwesha. So based on this truth which you see, You are seeing the distorted truth, and based on this distorted truth, you make analysis which also will be distorted.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: You take decisions which also will be distorted, and finally you take actions which naturally has to be wrong. So therefore what happens? You do. Paradharma, no, before raga comes, after raga comes moha. Moha means delusion. What is delusion? Delusion is that state of mind where you are not seeing the reality. You are seeing something other than the reality. Perverted vision is the end result of Moha. So based on this Moha, then you take wrong action, which we call as Paradharma. When wrong action happen, what is the result of wrong action? Shoka is the result, sorrow is the result.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: So why now in our own life you see, if there is sorrow in your life, just go back step by step and finally where you should land up. You will land up at agnana. I don't know myself, therefore I am in sorrow. Now this is the right way of analysis. This is how we have to analyze our life, analyze our problem, and this is how we have to come out of our problem. The scriptures teach us the way to think. The masters teach us the way to think, how to think, how to handle a situation.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: How to solve a problem, that way of thinking is what the scriptures do for us. So Arjuna, your sorrow is because of lack of self-knowledge. So therefore, I am going to give you that self-knowledge. So from verse number 12 to 25, Bhagwan is dealing with self-knowledge alone because this alone can put an end to suffering. It's a permanent end to suffering. There may be very many methods to end suffering. Short term methods, long term methods, impermanent methods, there may be so many means, but this method is the ultimate method, a permanent method. In fact, it even puts an end to the repeated cycle.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: sickles of birth and death. To such an extent, this is a permanent solution. So now how does Bhagwan begin? Bhagwan says, Arjuna, there was never a time when we were not there. We means I, you, and all these kings who have assembled here to fight. There was never a time in the past when we were not there. There will never be a time in the future when we all will not be there. Meaning, in the past also we were there. In the present also we are there, in the future also we will continue to be there.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Meaning what? We are all deathless. We are not talking of the body, we are talking of the supreme self, our true nature, which is of the nature of pure consciousness. This consciousness has no death. Bhagwan, how do you say so? Arjuna, it is your direct experience. Just analyze your experience. What is your experience? Every time your body is changing, as you grow old, the body is constantly changing. The childhood body is replaced by the youth body. Youth body is replaced by the old body. So constantly one after the other the body is changing, but are you changing?

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Are you the observer? Are you the witness of this change? Are you changing? The very fact that you are able to recollect all these changes, you are able to remember them. It shows you were there in the past, you are there in the present. Even when the bodies are changing, you, the witness is not changing. Pay attention to that truth in you, that consciousness in you, that awareness in you, who is just a witness of all these changes. And thus, start paying attention to that changeless awareness in you. Start holding on to that truth in you.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Pay attention to it, hold on to it. That is the real you. What happens if you hold on to it? Just like while living your body is constantly changing. So what will be the logical step in the next? Childhood body is replaced by the youth body. Youth body is replaced by the old body. And what happens next? A time has to come when the old body will have to drop. Now what will happen to the I, the witness in you? Till now the witness nothing has happened when the body has changed. So naturally nothing will happen even when the body drops dead because the consciousness in you has nothing to do with the body of yours.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Body is totally different, consciousness is totally different. There is no connection at all. Body's death is not your death. This consciousness you must hold on. It is this knowledge which makes a wise man, a pandita free from grief. It is this knowledge which makes a dheera free from delusion, moha. Because there is always this consciousness which is giving you everything you need. What is our desire? I don't want to die, I want to live forever and ever and ever, I want to exist all the time. This existence is the nature of yourself. It is the nature of consciousness.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: So you don't have to desire it, it is already there. Again, I have this desire that I should always be happy and peaceful. You don't have to desire it because the self in you is Ananda Swarupa. So the self in you is Sat Swarupa. The self in you is Chit Swarupa. The self in you is Ananda Swarupa. Whatever desire you have, In life, all these desires are already fulfilled in this self. So you don't have to desire it because it is your nature. Your nature means what? It can never leave you. It is the very I in you.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: It is the very aham in you. Bhagwan Shankaracharya says, even God cannot take it away from you. This aham is always available. The mistake you have done is you have never paid attention to it. You were, you were ignoring it. You are not experiencing it, not because it is not there, you are not experiencing it because you are ignoring it till now. That's why it is called self-ignorance. That which is ignored is called ignorance. So then what has to be done? Start paying attention to the reality in you. Then all this peace, happiness, everything will be your nature.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Bhagwan, now with this knowledge, how to live in this world? How can this knowledge help me in living in this world? This is the essence of the next two verses. Let us chant them. Matra sparshastu kaunteya sheetoshna sukha duhkhadaha agamapayino nityaha tansthitiksha Shashva Bharata Yam hi navyathayante te Purusham Purusharshabha Samadukha Sukham Dheeram Yes. So what is life? Life is a constant interaction between the sense organs and the sense objects. So here Bhagwan says, matra sparshah. What do you mean matra? Matra doesn't mean tablet. Matra. Ma means to measure. Tra means instrument. So what is Matra?

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: The instrument of measuring. Meeyante aabhi shabdaadayaha. Meeyante to measure. That instrument of measuring is called matra. Now what is that instrument we have to measure? The panchagyanendriyas. The five organs of knowledge through which We measure. Measure means what? We know. So it is like we with our eyes measure color and form. Meaning, we gain the knowledge of color and form. With our ears, we measure sound. Meaning, we know sound. So what are the panchajnanendriyas? Eyes. Ears, nose, tongue, skin. And what are the knowledge we gain from the world? Shabda, sparsha, roopa, rasa, gandha. Shabda, sound, we gain it through our ears.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Sparsha. Touch, the skin is the instrument. Roopa, form and color, we use our eyes. Shabda sparsha roopa rasa, taste, through our tongue, we gain that knowledge. Gandha, smell, we gain it through. our nose. So these are the panchajnanendriyas. So with the panchajnanendriyas you gain the knowledge from the outer world. If these panchajnanendriyas are not there, for such a person the world is not there. He'll be shut out from the world. So now, matra means the instruments of knowing. Matra sparsha. Sparsha means what? Contact. So matra sparsha means contacting instruments. Those instruments which are coming in contact with the respective sense objects.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: The sense organs, when they come in contact with their respective sense objects, this is the meaning Matra Sparsha. What will happen? When the instruments come in contact with the objects, sheet, ushna, sukha, dukha, dah. Dah means givers. They give. Da means to give. What do they give? Sheeta, ushna, sukha, dukha. Sheeta, cold, ushna, heat. Sukha, joy, dukha, sorrow. So when our self Sense organs come in contact with the sense objects. What do they give? What does this contact give? They give pairs of opposites. What are they? Sheeta ushna at the body level. Sukha dukha at the mind level.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Mana apamana at the intellect level. Meaning, you have no choice when the senses come in contact with the sense objects, you will experience ups and downs. All those things have to be understood, the pairs of opposites. Day and night. Victory and defeat. Ninda, stuti, praise, criticism. Health, disease, they're all pairs of opposites. What does Bhagwan say? You have no choice. These are all choiceless situations. So how to live in this world then? Understand they are Agama Apayanaha. Agama they come, Apayana they go and therefore Anityaha they are impermanent. All these experiences are impermanent, therefore what is the solution?

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Tan Titikshasva Bharata. Oh Bharata, there is only one way, Titikshasva, practice Titiksha. Endure them, cheerfully endure them. What is the definition of Titiksha? Sahanam sarva dukhanam apratikara poorvakam. Chinta vilapa rahitam satitiksha nigadyate. This is the definition given by Bhagwan Shankaracharya in Vivekachudamani. So what is titiksha? Sahanam is titiksha. Sahanam means what? Endurance. Endurance of what? Sarva dukhanam, all the sorrows. How should you endure all the sorrows? Up Pratikara poorvakam, without a feeling of revenge. There is no pratikara. Chinta vilapa rahitam, free from grumbling, free from wailing and weeping, free from complaining, without any grudge. Against anyone, chinta vilapa rahitam, sati diksha nigadyate, that is called titiksha.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: So as far as life is concerned, nobody has a choice. We are exposed to the ups and downs of life, everyone has to face it. Ups also will come, downs also will come. What is our only choice? The only choice is whether to grumblingly complain, or cheerfully endure. This is all our choice. Bhagwan says, choose the later. In life, 99% of the situations are choiceless. We don't say all situations are choiceless. There are choiceful situations also. So in such situation what should you do? Choose, what else? Why do you worry? Where there is a choice, choose.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Choose means work hard, try to get it. Where there is no choice, accept it cheerfully. This is the method. Why do you say 99% of the cases we are choiceless? How much choice do we have? Which body to be born, do we have any choice? What kind of body, do we have any choice? Which parents should we be born? We don't have a choice. Which place we should be born? We don't have a choice. Whether it should be a day or a night, we don't have any choice. The change of seasons, do we have any choice?

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: How the body should function, the heart, liver, kidney, how they should function, we don't have any choice. It is functioning, that's all. Isn't it? That is why Bhagwan takes only that case here. He's not taking the cases where there is a choice. He's taking the case where there is no choice. In life, in most of the situation, you will face a situation where there is no choice. So what should be our attitude? Cheerfully endure them. How to cheerfully endure? Understand it is Agamaha Apayanaha. Endure everything keeping this in mind. What is it? Whatever is there now, someday or the other, it will go away.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: It has to go away, it cannot remain with you. Mainly the sorrowful situations only worries us. As a famous English saying goes, even this will pass away. That is Agamaha Apayana. Everything in this world is Anitya, impermanent. Now we have to think a little, how to cheerfully endure the happenings of life. First technique is the same technique, just Understand that the bad patch of time which you are going through, someday or the other it will go away. It cannot remain with you for all the time because in this world everything is anitya. The second way of practicing Titiksha is understand that whatever you are going through is your own karma phala.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: You only have ordered it. So what you are going through is tailor made. You have performed some action in the past, the very same action has come. in the form of karma phala in the present. Don't blame the people around. They are not the cause, your karma is the cause. Accept it, there is no other way. Number three, always know that whatever is happening is happening for the good. This is another way of cheerful endurance. In the first two cases, cheerful endurance is not possible. Even this will pass away. It won't help. This is my karma phala, it won't help.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Somewhere you endure helplessly. To cheerfully accept a thing, you must always see the hidden hand of omniscient, omnipotent, omnipresent God in giving you that particular particular result or situation. There is a supreme Lord who is taking care of the whole world. He is Sarvajna, omniscient. He is Sarvashaktiman, omnipotent. A sarvavyapi omnipresent such a supreme Lord without whose command even a dust particle cannot move here or there. Without whose command even a blade of grass cannot move. When such a Lord is taking care of this entire cosmos. So if this is the kind of situation he has put me in, definitely there is a good purpose.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Some purpose which at present I am not able to understand. A noble purpose is definitely there. This is the way to think. God is my father and mother. Bhagwan himself says that, Pitaahamasya jagato mata dhata pitama. I am the father and mother of this whole universe. So when the father or the mother does something to the child, it is always for the good of the child. The child may not understand. With this attitude, you must face the situation, accept the situation. Look at these plants and trees etcetera. What all kinds of seasons they have to undergo.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Rainy season, summer season, storms, winter season. Isn't it? And then finally what is the result? Beautiful flowers, juicy fruits. They don't come just like that. That plant has endured so many ups and downs and as a result, the beautiful flower comes. The sweet fruit comes in the same way in our life also. You will always find that it is the suffering which makes you a noble person. Always. It is not the, it is not the what you call, good things that happen to you. When good things happen to you, you tend to become arrogant. When good things happen to you, you tend to become indifferent to other's sorrows.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: When good things happen to you, you tend to become careless. When good things happen to you, you tend to become ungrateful. Just observe. When suffering comes to you, just the opposite happens. When you go through suffering, you are at your best because you are absolutely alert. In that state of pain, you cannot remain in Tamas. When you are suffering, you become introspective. And a person who has suffered, when he sees the suffering of others, His heart melts in compassion because when he sees the other suffering, he is able to recollect his own suffering. Yes, I know this pain because I have gone through it.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: So then what happens? Your heart melts seeing the pain of others. And also you are filled with humility. You are filled with gratitude for God. There are so many things the pain can teach you. And that is why all those what you call people who have done bad karmas, they are sent to Naraka. All kinds of sufferings are there, descriptions are there. Now what is Naraka? It is nothing but a washing machine. You put all the soil close there. What comes out is dress clean and neat, isn't it? What happens there? When that criminal minded fellow suffers like this, it is that all the impurities of the mind gone.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: A person who suffers comes out to be a noble person. It can be physical suffering, it can be mental suffering. In fact, it is this suffering which brings you vairagya, dispassion. It is this suffering which makes your mumukshutvam intense. The desire for liberation becomes intense only during the moments of suffering. The best example is Bhagavad Gita. The suffering of Arjuna led to Bhagavad Gita, isn't it? In your own life if you see, it is always the suffering which has made you a better person. At the moment of suffering we can't accept this, no doubt. At the moment of suffering we may curse God, accept it.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: But after that, After that bad patch is gone, you always come out to be a better person. This is true with everyone. So therefore we say even the suffering is a blessing in disguise. That is why Kunti Mata prays for suffering, isn't it? What was her prayer? Vipada santu nashyashwata tatra tatra jagadguru bhavato darshanam yat syat apunarbhava darshanam. Bhagwan, vipadas santu na shashwatu, let vipat, calamities strike us again and again. Because it is only during the calamities that I sincerely from the depth of my heart, I seek you. And it is in those moments when I really experience your presence in my heart.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: And as a result, it is only this attunement with you which puts an end to the cycles of birth and death. So therefore, Bhagwan, keep giving me calamities alone. See the prayer of Kunti Mata, my God. All the great saints and all, whenever sufferings come to them, they say, Bhagwan, thank you very much. This is what they say. Thank you very much. So our attitude towards sorrow has to change. So what does Bhagwan say? You have no choice with the outer situation. Throw yourself at the mercy of the omnipotent, omniscient Lord. And when the sorrow come, what should be your attitude?

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Titikshasva, cheerfully endure, because whatever happens is for your happiness, for your welfare and well-being alone. But how to cheerfully endure, hold on to the permanent, this don't forget. Yam hi navyathayanti ete. Purusham purusharshabha. That person who is not afflicted by these ups and downs of life, shita ushna sukha dukha etcetera. Those people who don't get afflicted, vyathayanti. Ete, through this, through these pairs of opposites, that person who is sama dukha sukham, who is equanimous. Equipoised even amidst sukha or dukha, not getting elated when there is sukha, not getting dejected when there is dukha. He handles both the situations with a peaceful, equanimous mind.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Bhagwan says, such a person is dheera. The wisest man, saha amrutatvaya kalpate. Such a person is fit for amrutatvam, the state of immortality. Such a person alone is fit to realize the highest state. So what has to be done? Now this is the formula of life. In life, in this world, there are two things. What are they? One is the impermanent thing, the other is the permanent thing. So what is the secret of living a happy life? Hold on to the permanent, play in the realms of the impermanent. What is the secret? What is the permanent thing?

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: The self, the consciousness. It is Nitya. It is not Agamaha, Apayana, coming and going. No, everything else comes and goes, but there is one thing which just witnesses the coming and going of everything. What is it? Consciousness. Hold on to consciousness and then live your life in the realms of change. This is the secret of living a happy life. Constant change, Agamaha Apayanaha. What is that which is coming and going? Sense organs are coming and going. Sense objects are coming and going. Experiences are coming and going. But what doesn't come and go? The experiencer, the witness doesn't come and go.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Hold on to him for your existence, for your security, for your happiness. Holding on to it, you become cheerful, with that cheerful attitude, live in the world of change. This is the secret. Knowingly or unknowingly, we do this everywhere. When you are watching a movie in the theater, what are you doing? You're doing the same thing, isn't it? You very well know that whatever is happening in the movie is not going to affect me. There's a fire in the movie. You very well know that fire is not going to affect you, is it? That's why you are comfortably seated in the theater.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: There's a flood in the movie, you know it is not going to affect you. So how are you able to enjoy the movie? You are able to enjoy the movie by holding on to the reality, by holding on to the Nitya Vastu, then you enjoy the Anitya Vastu, isn't it? The very reason why you are enjoying the film is because in the film also you cry and weep and all that. In the theater you do that. But you enjoy even that crying. You even enjoy that sorrowful state, isn't it? Very strange. You are enjoying sorrow.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: You are enjoying crying and weeping. You are enjoying the moments of anxieties and fears and worries. How are you able to enjoy these fears and worries? You are able to enjoy because at the back of your mind, deep within, you are holding on to the reality. And what is the reality? I have nothing to do with that. That cannot affect me. I am different from that. The whole thing is an illusion. Because of this, you are able to enjoy the movie, isn't it? One part of the mind is holding on to the reality, another part of the mind is playing in the realms of change.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: This is the secret. Everywhere you do the same thing. You are playing chess. What is chess? It is nothing but war. There is a king. There is a queen, there is elephants, there are horses, there are soldiers and killing is happening. You are killing others, others are killing you, even in all these killings. What is happening to you? You are unaffected, isn't it? Because these killings are only mere imaginations. It is not real. In the real world, nothing is happening. Not even one drop of blood has come out. Isn't it? Always you see you are enjoying only when you are absolutely secure holding on to the reality, otherwise you can't enjoy.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: The 1 year old child makes his father a horse. The father readily becomes a horse. Now the child is sitting on the back. The child says, come on, eat grass and this father eats grass. No, he's a horse now on the floor. On all the floors he's crawling. Who? The father. The child is sitting on the back. Come on, drink water. The father drinks water. and makes all the sound of the horse also, to entertain the child, isn't it? So even when the father has become the horse, is he miserable? He's not miserable. Why? Because he knows I'm not horse.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Isn't it? In the drama also the same thing, you take up the role. You're ready to become a king or a beggar. wanting to become a wretched creature there. You do all kinds of things. Why are you able to do all this? Because at the back of the mind, you know, I have nothing to do with this role. I am somebody different. So when you have that knowledge, you are able to cheerfully do your role in the world. In the same way, we must know who we are. Without that, the life can be a tragedy.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Give importance to the permanent thing, never give importance to the impermanent. What happens when you give importance to the impermanent? Have you seen these people who commit suicide when India loses the match against Pakistan? The newspaper they come. It is the heights of madness. 11 plus 11 players are playing. Compared to the crowd of India which is in crores, what is this 11? Some insignificant number of players are playing in a very, very small, maybe 1 acre, 2 acre land. Now what is the size of India? And then in the newspaper it comes, India defeated dash.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: What has India to do with these 11 people? Meaningless. It is all your imagination, foolish imagination. Some 11 people taking a piece of wood and a ball and hitting. And now you are connecting it to India. Isn't it? And there are people who take it very seriously. Oh my God, India has lost the match. Now what is the purpose of living? Just commit suicide. The heights of foolishness, that which is absolutely silly and insignificant has been given the maximum value, the greatest value, greater than your life itself. And what is the result? Shoka is the result.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Isn't it? In our life also we do the same mistake. The most important thing is ignored. The most unimportant things are given the maximum value. And this we go on suffering in life. Bhagwan says shift your attention to the most important thing in you, the consciousness in you, which is always there, which is in fact waiting for you to turn your attention inward so that that consciousness can bless you. with peace, with happiness. That's why Swami Vivekananda said, arise, awake. Wake up, you are sleeping now. considering yourself to be this mere fleshy, filthy, perishable body.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: So what does Bhagwan say? Hold on to the permanent and what you call, play your role in the fields of the impermanent as Pujya Guruji used to say. Andhraama baahar drama, bas. Simple, Andhraama baahar drama. Now Bhagwan says, whoever is not affected by the ups and downs of the external world, na vyathayanti. Such a person is fit for that highest knowledge. Means what? This truth is always there in us. In order to experience this truth, you need a peaceful mind. And in order to have a peaceful mind, you must ensure that your mind is not affected by the ups and downs of life.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Remain quiet, remain peaceful, remain equanimous. Later on it will come. Samatvam yoga uchyate, real yoga means samatvam. Quietude of your mind is real yoga. Those people who can keep their mind undisturbed, peaceful at all times, Bhagwan says, he is a fit person for the highest. Why? Because to experience the highest, the only qualification necessary is a quiet mind. And this person has a quiet mind. So even in that state of utter misery, this person experiences the infinite and the immortal. person who can remain quiet, who can keep his mind peaceful, steady, such a person easily gets it.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: So Arjuna therefore, this is the way to live. Hold on to the real, play in the realms of the Impermanent. Now here, interestingly Bhagwan uses the two terms, Nitya and Anitya. Arjuna, this self in the past also it was there, in the present also it is there. In the future also it will be there. So therefore this self is Nitya Vastu. And everything else, the world, the body, the mind, the senses, everything is Anitya Vastu. So Arjuna, there are two things in this world, one is Nitya Vastu, Anitya Vastu. So what should be done? Hold on to the Nitya and Play your game in the Anitya, but Arjuna, do you know one thing?

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: Bhagwan, what is it? Actually, this division of Nitya Anitya is wrong. Then what is it, Bhagwan? It is actually Sat and Asat. What is the difference? Let us see the next verse. Na sato vidyate bhavah, na bhavo vidyate satah, ubhayorapi drushtontah, tvanyostatvadarshibhih. Yes, a very, very famous verse. In short, the entire message of the Upanishad is in a capsule form given in this. What is the message of the Upanishads? Now see what is said here. Asataha bhavaha na vidyate, first statement. Asataha bhavaha na vidyate. Asataha of the unreal bhavaha existence na vidyate is not there.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: The unreal doesn't exist. Statement number one. The unreal has no existence. Then statement number two. Sataha abhavaha na vidyate. Sataha of the real. Abhavaha, non-existence na vidyate is not there. Of the unreal, there is no non-existence. This is the second statement. What is the first statement? For the unreal, there is no existence. Second statement, for the real, there is no non-existence. Means what? Real always exist. Unreal never exists, bas. Tatvadarshibhihi, the seers of the truth. Tatva, tatva means what? Tat plus tvam is tatva. Tat means that. Tvam means ness, that ness. T H A T dash N E S S thatness.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: That is called Tatvam. Thatness means what? The truth of that. So Tatvadarshi means the one who is seeing the truth of a thing. Such a person is called Tatvadarshi. The same Pandita, Dheera, they're all different names. The wise man. who is seeing the reality as it is. For such a tatvadarshi, ubhayoho antah drishtaha. He has seen both. What are the two things? The real and the unreal. What is the nature of real? Real always exists. What is the nature of the unreal? Unreal never exists. Tatvadarshi has seen the truth, antah means the truth. He has seen the truth of both.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: He knows what is real, he knows what is unreal. Now very interestingly, till now Bhagwan was talking of nitya anitya, suddenly Bhagwan raises his level to Sat, Asat. Now what is the difference? When you say something is impermanent, somewhere you are giving reality to it, isn't it? This is impermanent means what? Ha, it remains for a short time, but it remains. It is real, at least for a short time it is real. So when you are saying something is anitya, You are not, you are not telling that it is unreal. You are telling it is real, at least for some time it is real, isn't it?

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: That's the difference between Anitya and Asat. When something is unreal, it never existed, either in the past or in the future or in the present, it is never there. Then that is called Asat. For example, the snake in the rope, Rajju Sarpa. In the past also the snake was not there. In the future also it is, it will not be there, in the present also it is, it was never there. That is called Asat. Are you able to distinguish? When you say Anitya, what does it mean? Like a flower, it is there, but for some time.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: There is a time wise limitation, but it is real, that is called Anitya. Now Bhagwan says, actually speaking Arjuna, the world which you see is not Anitya, actually it is Asat. One more level he goes higher. I have told you Anitya because you may not be able to digest it. You may not be able to accept what? This body is Anitya, world is Anitya, but I'm experiencing, you may say that, but the fact is a fact. The world doesn't even exist. is Asat. Then what is Sat? The consciousness alone is Sat. Other than consciousness, everything is Asat, everything is unreal.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: This truth Tatvadarshi knows. Therefore, as far as a Tatvadarshi is concerned, he need not do Titiksha. Who has to do Titiksha? The one who considers world to be real, he has to do Titiksha. As far as a Tatvadarshi is concerned, there is no thing at all. Then what would what? What is that Titiksha then? Titiksha means enduring. That which doesn't even exist, where is the question of endurance? This is the level of a Gnani. Whatever we have discussed earlier, it is at the level of a Sadhaka. For a Sadhaka, things are explained as Nitya and Anitya.

speaker: Swami Aparajitananda
text: For a Gyani, things are very clear. What is the clarity? It is not Nitya Anitya, it is Sat Asat. Bhagwan, I understand that this consciousness is nitya, etcetera. But what about the world? How can you say this world is unreal? How can you say that? Let us chant the next words. Avinashitu tadviddhi yena sarvamidam tatam vinashamavyayasyasya na kashchit kartumarhati.
